title: SAEmnesia: Erasing Concepts in Diffusion Models with Supervised Sparse Autoencoders
claim: Binding each concept to one latent lets us erase a target by steering a single unit, leaving unrelated content intact.
layout: 2 stacked panels: top schematic with annotations, bottom 3x4 image grid with dashed divider
description: The figure has two stacked parts. The top is a schematic. A prompt, "An image of Architectures in Abstractionism style", with the concept words in red and blue, feeds a green Diffusion Model block. Beside the block, a vertical axis of SAE activations shows small black bars, with one red bar and one blue bar highlighted. Arrows from the highlighted bars point to two annotations: "each latent is active for a single concept → monosemanticity" and "each concept is mapped to a single latent → feature centralization". The bottom is a 3x4 grid of stylized generated images. Rows are prompts: Architectures in Picasso style, Bears in Blossom Season style, and Sandwiches in Van Gogh style. Columns are "SD w/o SAE", separated by a dashed line from the three concepts erased with SAEmnesia: Architectures, Bears and Sandwiches. In the diagonal cells the target object disappears while the style stays. The eye goes first to the colorful image grid.
caption: SAEmnesia enables precise concept-level manipulation: each latent activates for a single concept (monosemanticity), and each concept is embedded in a single latent (feature centralization). So, to erase a target concept, we only need to steer a single latent. The removed concepts correctly disappear in the diagonal images ("Architectures", "Bears", "Sandwiches") while the corresponding style is preserved. Note that they remain present in the non-diagonal ones, thereby preserving the fidelity and diversity when unlearning unrelated content.
abstract: Concept unlearning in diffusion models is hampered by feature splitting, where concepts are distributed across many latent features, making their removal challenging and computationally expensive. We introduce SAEmnesia, a supervised sparse autoencoder framework that overcomes this by enforcing one-to-one concept-neuron mappings. By systematically labeling concepts during training, our method achieves feature centralization, binding each concept to a single, interpretable neuron. This enables highly targeted and efficient concept erasure. Compared to the state-of-the-art sparse autoencoder-based unlearning approach, SAEmnesia reduces hyperparameter search by 96.67% and achieves a 9.22% improvement on the UnlearnCanvas benchmark for objects. Our method also shows superior scalability in sequential unlearning, improving accuracy by 28.4% when removing nine objects, establishing a step forward for precise and controllable concept erasure. Moreover, SAEmnesia effectively suppresses nudity on the I2P benchmark and remains robust to adversarial attacks. Source code available at https://github.com/EIDOSLAB/SAEmnesia.
